$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT agent organization for a fresh installation.
The capability layer resolves the initiating actor from the declared
org before it will answer any bridge action; with no org it refuses
with BRIDGE_ACTOR_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE. The builder's own org names
the builder's seats, accounts and account lanes, which are personal
data and are meaningless on a customer's machine. So the build stages
THIS file in its place.
WHY THIS FILE DECLARES SEATS, AND WHY IT USED TO DECLARE ONE.
It previously carried the controller alone, on the reasoning that a
fresh install has no org to describe and that binding a provider is a
setup step rather than a shipped assumption. That reasoning was right
about providers and wrong about seats, and the cost was total: the
bridge resolves a dispatch by finding a declared agent whose id and
provider match the requested tier, so with no codex or claude agent
declared, EVERY dispatch on EVERY packaged install refused with
BRIDGE_AGENT_DECLARATION_MISSING. The product could not start an agent
at all. It worked for us only because the builder's own org declares
twenty agents -- so no source test could ever catch it, and no amount
of testing on a development machine would have.
A seat is a DECLARATION, not a claim about the customer's machine.
The fleet view renders declared agents and the surrounding copy already
forces the declared-versus-observed distinction, so declaring a seat a
person has no credentials for is consistent with what the graph already
promises it means. `provider` here names which CLI a seat would use if
the person installs and signs into it; the controller stays "none"
because it is this product, not an external tool.
EVERY FIELD BELOW IS LOAD-BEARING.
enabled MUST be true. The lane resolver matches on id and provider
only and never reads `enabled`, so a disabled seat passes that check
and then dies further in with LAUNCH_DISABLED_AGENT -- a refusal
written for a different situation, reaching a person who did nothing
wrong.
Every seat needs its `manages` edge. A codex seat without one refuses
outright (BRIDGE_AGENT_REPORTING_LINE_MISSING); a claude seat would
survive, because it falls back to the enabled controller. They are
declared anyway, because termination authorises through the DECLARED
management graph -- a seat with no edge becomes un-terminable whenever
no live presence row exists for it.
Astra is the default tier for new circles. Its declared Codex seat
and controller edge are required by the same allocator as Luna, Terra
and Sol; offering its model without this seat refuses fresh installs.
FOUR claude seats, not one. All three Claude tiers share this pool,
and the presence registry refuses a second live lane per identity, so
a single `claude` identity capped the product at ONE concurrent Claude
agent no matter which tier was asked for. Four ids is what makes a
four-agent fleet possible; the tier table allocates a free one.
assertSingleController() requires exactly one enabled controller, so
this file must always carry exactly one.
THE CONTROLLER STAYS NEUTRAL. agent.spawn binds the authenticated
transport actor to a fresh dispatch-only projection; it does not stamp
Codex, Claude or Gemini into this persistent declaration. The
Claude worker pool therefore starts at claude-1, leaving the principal
name claude available without choosing it as the controller.
